reference: GNU getent passwd on the harness-generated runner account, projected to uid:gid:gecos:home:shell, is the independent oracle for the runnable lookup parity case. The harness reference namespace has a synthetic passwd database and files-only NSS configuration. Contract expectations for Bash metadata and the custom userdb API come from its documented help contract and POSIX passwd field ordering; no expectation is derived from candidate output. The custom provider and authentication APIs have no matching GNU CLI.
coverage: Bash reports userdb as a builtin and exposes its documented help synopsis.
GNU getent comparison for the harness-generated runner passwd record, projected to the five fields returned by userdb lookup.
Contract lookup using a relative private passwd fixture, including empty GECOS and shell fields.
Contract not-found status and empty-config built-in provider listing.
Private malformed-record skipping, first valid match and invalid output-variable rejection.
exclusions: No installed or real account database, password, shadow entry, or authentication credential is read or changed.

Built-in password verification, external provider execution, provider registration/removal, provider error handling, and LDAP password-fd behavior are deferred for isolated disposable fixtures and mocks.

cases.purpose: Compare userdb's five-field record for the harness's synthetic runner account with GNU getent passwd. The reference branch projects away the name and password fields; this account exists only in the isolated harness metadata.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t userdb) == builtin ]]; then
  userdb lookup runner -V record
  printf '%s\n' "$record"
else
  entry=$(getent passwd runner)
  IFS=: read -r name passwd uid gid gecos home shell <<< "$entry"
  printf '%s:%s:%s:%s:%s\n' "$uid" "$gid" "$gecos" "$home" "$shell"
fi

cases.purpose: Check that Bash resolves the loadable through its builtin type metadata.
Check the Bash help entry contains the documented lookup, verification, provider-management synopsis, and provider deadline without invoking those operations.
cases.script:
help userdb > help.txt
help_text=$(<help.txt)
[[ $help_text == *"userdb lookup USER -V VAR"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"userdb verify USER PASSWORD"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"userdb add-provider NAME PATH [ARGS...]"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"Provider exchange (including password input) has a five-second deadline."* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented help entries present\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented uid:gid:gecos:home:shell result preserves empty GECOS and shell fields from a small relative private passwd fixture.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'fixture:x:4242:4343::home-fixture:' > users.fixture
: > providers.fixture
BASHUSERDB_PASSWD=users.fixture BASHUSERDB_CONF=providers.fixture userdb lookup fixture -V answer
printf '%s\n' "$answer"

cases.purpose: Check the documented rc 1 for a missing user when the private passwd fixture and provider configuration are empty; the diagnostic is intentionally checked only for being present.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'fixture:x:4242:4343:Fixture:home-fixture:shell-fixture' > users.fixture
: > providers.fixture
rc=0
BASHUSERDB_PASSWD=users.fixture BASHUSERDB_CONF=providers.fixture userdb lookup absent -V answer || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]] || exit 1
printf 'missing status=%s\n' "$rc"
